newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi shares slip 2.2 pct after US attack on Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Delhi shares slip 2.2 pct after US attack on Iraq.

text.p: Delhi shares closed sharply lower, shedding more than two percent as news of a U.S. missile strike against Iraq unsettled the bourse, brokers said.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index, which had opened moderately higher, closed 17.91 points, or 2.2 percent, lower at 789.68.
Traders called the fall in prices a reflex reaction to the latest crisis involving Iraq.
"Large-scale panic selling by foreign institutional investors completely reversed the early rising trends," said Pradeep Sharma of brokers Surge Investments.
Brokers said the market was caught off guard by news the United States had launched cruise missile strikes against air defence targets in Iraq in retaliation for Iraqi military attacks against Kurds.
The news injected uncertainty into the market and raised fears of a rise in commodity prices, especially oil, they said.

But some predicted the decline in prices would be temporary. "I expect the market to stage some recovery very soon as domestic financial institutions have been active and making substantial purchases," a broker said.

Widespread expectations that the government will relax a proposed minimum corporate tax had underpinned prices over the past several sessions. But news of the U.S. attacks on Iraq prompted short selling by speculators, they said.
Finance Minister P. Chidambaram on Tuesday postponed a statement on the proposed 1996/97 (April-March) budget because of upheaval in parliament over political developments in a western state.

A senior aide to the minister said the finance minister, who had been expected to discuss the proposed budget before the lower house of parliament on Tuesday afternoon, would possibly make the statement on Wednesday.
Reliance Industries lost 6.55 rupees to 208.85, while TISCO fell 5.90 rupees to 195.70 on panic selling by foreign institutional investors and speculators, brokers said.
State Bank of India dropped 6.20 rupees to 277.75, while ACC quoted 45 rupees down at 2,175.
TELCO was down 19.50 rupees to 502.50 and ITC tumbled to 296 rupees, 2.80 lower.
